text:
Today TaxDome has a vendor-neutral `TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations` core with a convention-based adapter boundary. **Instead is the only registered adapter.** `juno`, `gruntworx`, and `instead` exist in the database enum, but Juno remains outside these ports and GruntWorx’s enum value does not constitute an integration. See [Registry](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/registry.rb:3) and [FirmSettings](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/firm_settings.rb:5).

**Vendor-neutral ports**

The ports are ordinary Ruby services and concerns, rather than a formally declared interface:

| Area | Core responsibility |
|---|---|
| Authorization and connections | Start/complete connection ceremonies; find, disconnect, revoke, renew, and verify grants. |
| Export | Authorize access, validate documents against capabilities, create/reuse the tax-preparation envelope and send records, then delegate delivery. |
| Status ingestion | Accept adapter-translated processing statuses and failure reasons; enforce transitions and broadcast changes. |
| Recovery | Resume eligible failed sends after reconnecting; sweep stale sends for reconciliation; keep idle grants alive. |
| Lifecycle | Clean up firm/client/contact data and merge contact-related records. |
| Shared infrastructure | OAuth token handling, HTTP transport/errors, presigned byte transfer, and capability validation. |

The central export boundary is particularly clear: core opens the shared records and calls the adapter with them; the adapter owns the vendor workflow. Rejected files are returned individually, and an export with no accepted files never reaches the adapter. [ExportAsync](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:53)

Adapters translate vendor statuses into the common vocabulary before calling `Documents::UpdateStatus`; that service applies the state machine and broadcasts after commit. [UpdateStatus](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/documents/update_status.rb:3)

**How an adapter plugs in**

Registration is static:

```ruby
ADAPTERS = { instead: TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead }.freeze
FEATURE_FLAGS = { instead: :tax_automations_instead }.freeze
```

The registry resolves the current provider from `FirmSettings`, or an explicitly named provider during connection/switching. Unknown providers raise `UnknownProviderError`. A missing feature-flag entry means the provider is offered to every firm. Existing connection rows resolve their client through their own namespace, preserving vendor identity after a firm switches. [Registry](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/registry.rb:10)

Actual production dispatch sites require the adapter namespace to provide:

| Namespace member | Required contract |
|---|---|
| `Connection` | Firm association and queryable connection rows; `.for_firm(firm)`, `.usable_for(firm)`, `.capabilities`, and the shared OAuth lifecycle/storage contract. |
| `Client` | Constructible with a connection; supports shared token renewal/revocation and applicable transport operations. Instead subclasses `BaseClient`, which includes `TokenRefreshable`. |
| `Authorizations::Create` | `.call(user, actor, provider, return_url)` → service result containing the authorization URL. |
| `Connections::Create` | `.call(user, actor, provider, params)` → service result containing the connection. |
| `ExportAsync` | `.call(user, actor, tax_preparation, tax_automation_documents:)`. Also used when resuming sends. |
| `Documents::ReconcileStatusesAsync` | `.call(user, actor, connection, {tax_automation_document_ids: ...})`; required by the background reconciliation sweep. |
| `DestroyForTaxPreparations` | `.call(user, actor, firm_id, tax_preparations)`. |
| `DestroyForFirm` | `.call(user, actor, firm_id)`. |
| `MergeForContact` | `.call(user, actor, firm_id, source_contact_id, target_contact_id)`. |

These requirements come from the [authorization port](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/authorizations/create.rb:35), [connection callback](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/connections/create.rb:138), [export dispatch](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:207), [reconciliation worker](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/documents/reconcile_sweep_worker.rb:34), and lifecycle services for [envelopes](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/tax_preparations/batch_destroy.rb:50), [firms](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/firms/destroy_cleanup.rb:55), and [contact merges](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/tax_preparations/merge_for_contact.rb:91).

This boundary currently assumes **OAuth connections**. `HasOauthConnection` supplies encrypted-token integration and `disconnected / connected / expired / revoked` states; `TokenRefreshable` centralizes exchanges using adapter-declared OAuth settings. It is therefore not yet an authentication-agnostic plugin interface. [Connection concern](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/concerns/tax_preparation/tax_automations/has_oauth_connection.rb:3), [OAuth declaration](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/token_refreshable.rb:63)

**The capability passport**

`Connection.capabilities` returns a validated `HasCapabilities::Capabilities` value describing the **vendor**, independent of any connection row:

```text
terms[]
  return_type
  accepted_file_formats[]
  max_file_size_mb
supported_tax_years[]
```

Terms are per return type, allowing different formats or limits for different forms. Supported return types are derived from the terms. Adapters implement private class methods `capability_terms` and `supported_tax_years`; missing implementations or malformed values fail when `.capabilities` is called. Duplicate return-type declarations are rejected. [HasCapabilities](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/has_capabilities.rb:3)

Instead derives its supported forms from its entity mapping, takes formats/size limits from settings, and supports the current year plus the preceding two years. [Instead capabilities](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/connection.rb:72)

Core uses the passport to reject unsupported forms, years, extensions, and oversized files. The API exposes it as `return_types` with display metadata, `file_types`, `file_size_limit`, and `tax_years`. [Validation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export/validate_documents.rb:40), [Serialization](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/serializers/tax_preparation/base/tax_automations/connection_serializer.rb:57)

**Data model**

| Model | Meaning and important keys |
|---|---|
| `FirmSettings` | One row per firm: chosen provider and external vendor-account binding. |
| `TaxAutomations::TaxPreparation` | Shared filing envelope: firm, CRM client, optional contact, year, return type, EIN, business name. Still physically stored in `juno_tax_preparations`. |
| `TaxAutomations::Document` | Shared send record joining a source document, envelope, provider, and return type; owns upload/processing states and failure reason. |
| `Instead::Connection` | One grant per firm, with staff creator, encrypted tokens, expiry/lifecycle timestamps, external connection UUID, and PKCE ceremony state. |
| `Instead::Entity` | Vendor taxpayer/entity identity: external UUID, entity type, optional CRM client/contact linkage, source, names, synchronization/archive timestamps. |
| `Instead::Document` | Vendor extension of one shared send record: Instead entity, external file UUID, and upload path. |

Two details matter for future adapters:

- **The envelope key excludes provider and return type:** it is `(firm, client, contact, year)`. A later export can update its current return type. Each send record separately snapshots provider and return type, with uniqueness across `(firm, envelope, source document, provider, return type)`. [Envelope lookup](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/tax_preparations/find_or_create.rb:95), [send-record constraint](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/db/migrate/20261016125400_scope_tax_preparation_tax_automations_documents_to_return_type.rb:6)
- **Upload and processing are separate axes:** upload is `waiting / uploading / uploaded / failed`; processing is `sent / processing / processed / error / archived / exceeded`. Vendor handles belong in adapter tables; common lifecycle state belongs on the shared send record. [Shared document](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/document.rb:3), [Instead document](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/document.rb:3)

The remaining Juno table name and Juno-specific associations show that the shared model is still in a transitional state. GruntWorx can use the existing core boundary, but needs the complete namespace contract—including reconciliation and cleanup—and its authentication flow must fit or extend the current OAuth assumptions.
